subject: SDLC artifact bundle and mapping for SIG assessment
messages:
From: Harper Miller <harper@trustassess.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG questionnaire follow-up — request for SDLC artifacts

Naomi,

Thanks again for the quick intro last week. As part of the SIG intake for Acme Financial we need a compact bundle of SDLC evidence that maps to the SIG Control Family (Secure Development Lifecycle). To keep the assessor's work scoped, could you provide the following within the next 10 business days?

- Code review process docs and an export of reviewer history for the last 6 months (PR metadata preferred)
- CI/CD gating evidence: pipeline definitions, a recent successful run log, and branch protection config
- Secrets handling summary: ephemeral credential usage, vault/KMS rotation reports, where secrets are injected into pipelines
- Change management proof: sample change ticket, approval trail, and rollback checklist

If you can bundle non-sensitive artifacts into a single zip and provide a Drive link + manifest CSV, that would be ideal. If anything is too sensitive we can accept redacted screenshots with callouts.

Also let me know if you'd like a short call to walk through the mapping.

Best,
Harper Miller
Principal Assessor
TrustAssess

(Attachment: sig_control_matrix_template.xlsx - sample template for mapping)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Harper Miller <harper@trustassess.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 2 Sep 2025 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire follow-up — request for SDLC artifacts

Harper —

Appreciate the clear list. We can deliver a scoped bundle that covers all four bullets. High-level plan below and an ask for anything else you want included:

What we will provide (initial bundle):
- rdw_sdlc_artifact_index.csv (manifest mapping SIG controls to file names/PRs/pipeline runs)
- pr-review-snapshots.zip (exported PR comment threads and reviewer ids; redacted where necessary)
- ci_pipeline_run_20250904.log (example pipeline run: lint/test/build/deploy steps)
- kms_key_rotation_report.pdf (last rotation audit for the keys used to sign CI artifacts)

Notes / constraints:
- We will not include full binary artifacts or private keys. KMS reports can be redacted for key IDs if required.
- Some PRs reference internal bug IDs that are NDA-bound for a partner; we will include redacted PR diffs + reviewer metadata for those.

Request: Do you need the branch protection settings themselves (e.g., GitHub branch rules export), or is a screenshot + policy text sufficient?

If that works, we'll aim to drop a Drive link with the bundle and the manifest by EOD Friday (2025-09-05). If you prefer a quick 30-min walk-through, I can put time on the calendar — copying Marissa to coordinate artifacts from infra.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Head of Trust Operations
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: none)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Sep 2025 14:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG questionnaire follow-up — request for SDLC artifacts

Adding the infra/engineering details for the bundle:

Marissa here — a few clarifications for the assessor mapping so we can avoid back-and-forth:

1) Code review evidence
- We will include a CSV of PR metadata (PR id, author, merged_by, reviewers, primary reviewer, review timestamps, merge commit SHA). See example rows included in rdw_sdlc_artifact_index.csv.
- For protected branches we will include an exported policy snapshot (JSON) and a brief note describing external contributor rules.

2) CI/CD controls
- The pipeline run log (ci_pipeline_run_20250904.log) is from our canonical build pipeline (git->CI->staging deploy). It shows gated jobs that require review approvals and artifact signature verification.
- We will also include a short pipeline YAML with comments explaining gates (we will redact internal endpoints).

3) Secrets and KMS
- We use an ephemeral credential broker in CI: short-lived credentials are minted per job. We will include an architectural diagram (redacted) and the KMS rotation audit (kms_key_rotation_report.pdf).
- Secrets access is audited in our central audit log; we'll include an excerpt and a pointer to the full audit stream (security will vet redaction).

4) Change management
- Sample ticket: SEC-4821 (Jira) with approval trail, link to runbook, and rollback checklist. We'll attach exported comment history and approval timestamps.

I'll prepare the Drive bundle and manifest. Naomi — if you want me to push to the shared Drive folder, I will do that and ping Harper with the link.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Engineering Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

(Attachments referenced: pipeline-gated-jobs.yaml (redacted), sdlc_arch_diagram_redacted.png)

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Harper Miller <harper@trustassess.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 7 Sep 2025 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: SDLC artifact bundle delivered — mapping + access

Harper —

We uploaded the artifact bundle and manifest to the shared Drive folder. Items included (non-sensitive exports and redacted material where applicable):

- rdw_sdlc_artifact_index.csv (manifest mapping SIG controls -> files/PRs/pipeline runs)
- pr-review-snapshots.zip (exported PR threads; reviewer ids intact, sensitive diffs redacted)
- ci_pipeline_run_20250904.log (complete run log for the canonical pipeline)
- pipeline-gated-jobs.yaml (redacted pipeline definition with comments on gates)
- kms_key_rotation_report.pdf (audit summary for rotation events; key identifiers redacted)
- SEC-4821_export.json (sample change ticket with approval timestamps and rollback checklist)

Drive link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/sdlc-artifacts-2025
Manifest checksum: sha256:3a7f6c9d8b4f2e5c9f1b1e3c6d5a2f0b8c9e7a6d5c4b3a2f1e0d9c8b7a6e5f4d

A few quick notes for your review:
- The PR metadata ties reviewer IDs to internal usernames; if you need email addresses for reviewer verification we can provide a separate mapping under an NDA.
- The pipeline run shows our policy enforcement: required reviews, lint/test gating, and artifact signature checks — this should map to SIG-DEV-5 (review gate) and SIG-OPS-3 (artifact signing).
- KMS rotation reports are summary-level; if the assessor needs key-level rotation timestamps we will schedule a secure transfer via our compliance portal.

If you'd like a live 30-min walkthrough next week to walk through the manifest and point to specific PRs/pipeline segments, I'm available Tue/Wed morning PST.

Thanks — looking forward to your feedback.

Naomi Feldman
Head of Trust Operations
Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

(Attachments: rdw_sdlc_artifact_index.csv, pr-review-snapshots.zip, ci_pipeline_run_20250904.log, kms_key_rotation_report.pdf)
